scope: Historically attested New Zealand motifs for three fictional Fallout cosmetic identities
source_image_note: No page images were retained because the referenced official pages and collections carry Crown copyright, publisher conditions, or protected emblem restrictions. Final flags must use a separate ImageGen source master constrained by this research.

sources.title: New Zealand flag
sources.publisher: Manatu Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage
sources.source_date_or_range: Flag design 1869, formal description 1902, current guidance page updated 2023
sources.license_or_rights: Crown copyright and official government reference. Use factual geometry and colour guidance only. Do not copy page imagery or claim government endorsement.
claims_used: Royal blue field
Four five-pointed red stars with white borders on the fly
Flag proportion 1:2
Official reproduction colours white, Pantone 186C red, Pantone 280C blue
Star placement and relative star sizes are prescribed by the 1902 description
sources.uncertainty: The Fallout variants are fictional and are not official New Zealand flags. They must remain visibly distinct from the protected national flag design.

sources.title: The NZ flag, maritime origins
sources.publisher: Manatu Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage, NZHistory
sources.license_or_rights: Government history reference. Use historical facts and design lineage only. Do not reuse the page image without checking permission.
claims_used: Colonial government ships used Blue Ensign conventions
NZ initials were used briefly in 1867
Four red stars with white borders replaced the initials in 1869
The Southern Cross flag began as a maritime device before wider land use
sources.uncertainty: The fictional package can echo maritime continuity without reproducing the Union Jack canton or legal ensign unchanged.

sources.title: Flags of New Zealand, other official flags
sources.publisher: Manatu Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage, NZHistory
sources.source_date_or_range: Red Ensign adopted 1903, merchant use documented from 1899
sources.license_or_rights: Government history reference. Use the documented red field, white Southern Cross, and merchant maritime association as design research only.
claims_used: New Zealand Red Ensign is based on the British Red Ensign
Current design was introduced in 1903
White disc and four red Southern Cross stars were used to identify New Zealand merchant ships in 1899
The Red Ensign can be flown on land on occasions of Maori significance under New Zealand practice
sources.uncertainty: A generated Pacific Relief Republic flag must not be mistaken for the official Red Ensign. Omit the Union Jack and use a distinct canton or central relief emblem.

sources.title: Wearing the silver fern
sources.publisher: Te Ara Encyclopedia of New Zealand
sources.source_date_or_range: Silver fern use documented from the 1888 New Zealand Natives rugby tour onward
sources.license_or_rights: Te Ara text is generally CC BY-NC 4.0. The linked photograph is subject to New Zealand Herald permission and must not be copied. Use the historical fact and an original drawn fern only.
claims_used: Cyathea dealbata is the silver fern
Silver fern is an important unofficial national emblem
The motif appears on representative sports badges, military uniforms and graves, and meat and dairy export marks
sources.uncertainty: Silver fern is culturally broad but is not a statutory national flag emblem. Do not imply that a specific commercial silver fern trademark is being reproduced.

sources.title: Southern Cross
sources.publisher: Te Ara Encyclopedia of New Zealand
sources.source_date_or_range: Constellation source is enduring. Page published 2009
sources.license_or_rights: Te Ara text is generally CC BY-NC 4.0. Use the described constellation and navigation facts, not page imagery.
claims_used: Four bright stars outline the cross, with a fainter fifth star nearby
New Zealand flag uses four stars rather than the Australian five-star representation
The constellation is used for navigation toward south
Maori traditions include anchor or sky canoe interpretations, with variation by iwi
sources.uncertainty: Do not add the fifth Australian star to a New Zealand identity. Do not assign one Maori interpretation to all iwi.

sources.title: Civil Defence Emergency Management Regulations 2003, Schedule 1
sources.license_or_rights: Legislative text is a public legal reference. The official Civil Defence logo is regulated. Do not copy or alter the logo without authorization.
claims_used: Colour logo is a yellow triangle in a blue circle with CD lettering and CIVIL DEFENCE wording
Specified print colours are Pantone 294 blue and Process Yellow
Black and white version is a white triangle in a black circle with black CD lettering and white wording
sources.uncertainty: The logo is not a generic rescue badge. Use only as a colour and emergency-management reference. Remove CD lettering and avoid the exact circle-triangle lockup in fictional flags.

sources.title: Resolution A.760(18), Symbols related to life-saving appliances and arrangements
sources.source_date_or_range: Adopted 4 November 1993 under SOLAS related signage
sources.license_or_rights: Official IMO resolution. Use the existence, categories, and colour convention as design research. Do not present a fictional flag as an official safety sign.
claims_used: Lifeboat, rescue boat, liferaft, lifebuoy, lifebuoy with line, and lifebuoy with light or smoke are defined categories
Recommended emergency-equipment symbols are white on green
White direction arrows may be used on green when indicating equipment or stations
sources.uncertainty: A flag may use an original lifeboat or wave silhouette inspired by this vocabulary, but must not reproduce an exact ISO or IMO safety sign with operational meaning.

sources.title: Maritime Rules Part 23, Operating Procedures and Training
sources.license_or_rights: New Zealand government maritime rules. Use the distress-signal facts as reference only. Do not imply a fictional flag is an active distress signal.
claims_used: Red flare or red light indicates distress
Orange smoke is a distress signal
Orange canvas with a black square and circle or another appropriate symbol is used for identification from the air
NZ maritime rules connect vessels with government search and rescue services
sources.uncertainty: The orange and black locator language is operational. It can inform a small rescue accent, but an exact square-circle panel should not be placed on a national flag.

sources.title: Tino rangatiratanga flag
sources.publisher: Manatu Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage
sources.source_date_or_range: Designed 1989, unveiled at Waitangi 6 February 1990, Cabinet recognition 14 December 2009
sources.license_or_rights: Official cultural guidance. The flag has preferred national Maori status and specific display protocol. Use as a cultural reference only, not as decorative clip art.
claims_used: Black top, red bottom, and a white central koru are the documented layout
Koru represents an unfurling fern and renewal
The design is a preferred national Maori flag and can complement the New Zealand flag
The top of the koru is closest to the flagpole when displayed
sources.uncertainty: There is no approval to place the Tino Rangatiratanga layout on the Fallout variants. Use a koru only for a route with explicit Maori partnership and cultural review.

sources.title: Coastguard, Our Mission and History
sources.source_date_or_range: First official lifeboat at Timaru 1864, permanent Sumner rescue service 1898, current organisation ongoing
sources.license_or_rights: Organisation history and current branding are not a permission to reuse Coastguard logos, chevrons, names, or marks. Use only the documented history of volunteer maritime rescue.
claims_used: Coastguard Tautiaki Moana is New Zealand's primary maritime search and rescue organisation
Independent rescue services formed in the late nineteenth century
Lifeboat and volunteer rescue history supports a lifeboat-state identity
sources.uncertainty: Do not reproduce the current Coastguard logo, bow-wave symbol, chevron, or bilingual wordmark. Use a newly authored emblem.

sources.title: The emblems
sources.publisher: International Committee of the Red Cross
sources.source_date_or_range: International humanitarian law and emblem guidance, page updated 2015 and later
sources.license_or_rights: Red Cross, Red Crescent, and Red Crystal emblems are protected. ICRC text and images are not a source asset license.
claims_used: Red Cross, Red Crescent, and Red Crystal carry protected humanitarian and medical meanings
Unauthorized imitations can be misuse and can weaken the protective meaning
A general humanitarian state is not automatically entitled to use a protected emblem
sources.uncertainty: The Pacific Relief Republic must not use a red cross, red crescent, red crystal, or a close imitation. Use maritime rescue imagery instead.

sources.title: Flags, Emblems, and Names Protection Act 1981
sources.license_or_rights: Legislative text is a public legal reference. It is not permission to imply official government use.
claims_used: The New Zealand Ensign is declared the New Zealand Flag
The flag is the symbol of the Realm, Government, and people of New Zealand
Unauthorized alteration or a close imitation of the flag is an offence surface
The Red Ensign may be authorized for maritime significance
sources.uncertainty: Fictional flags must be visibly distinct from the exact official flag and should be framed as Fallout route identities rather than official state reproductions.

identity_briefs.concept: Continuity maritime remnant that treats the islands as a shared lifeboat
recommended_motifs: Deep royal-blue field informed by Pantone 280C New Zealand flag blue
Four red five-pointed Southern Cross stars with white borders, retaining New Zealand star count and orientation but moving the emblem so the result is not the official flag
Original silver or white silver-fern frond based on Cyathea dealbata, placed as the principal civic emblem
Optional narrow white sea line or small blue-and-white maritime device that does not copy a government ensign
avoid: Exact current New Zealand flag proportions and star placement
Coastguard logo or current rescue chevron
Tino Rangatiratanga black-red-white layout unless a Maori partnership route is explicitly approved
identity_briefs.orientation: If the Southern Cross is retained, keep the four-star cross legible and upright as a New Zealand reference. Keep the fern upright with the stem toward the lower hoist or lower centre, not mirrored.

palette.fern_silver: Neutral silver or white, not a claimed official Pantone value

identity_briefs.uncertainty: No Fallout-era or alternate New Zealand Lifeboat State flag is historically attested. This is a constrained fictional synthesis.

identity_briefs.concept: Open-port humanitarian republic that turns merchant and rescue traditions into a Pacific relief mandate
recommended_motifs: Red field or red maritime band referencing the New Zealand Red Ensign tradition
White four-star Southern Cross, visibly distinct from the official Red Ensign by omitting the Union Jack and using a new central composition
A small original white lifeboat, rescue boat, or lifebuoy silhouette in a green or sea-green roundel inspired by IMO A.760(18) life-saving categories
A restrained blue or teal wave band to signal Pacific routes
Optional silver fern as a small secondary mark, not a large sports or export trademark copy
avoid: Exact New Zealand Red Ensign with Union Jack canton
Red Cross, Red Crescent, Red Crystal, or any close imitation
Exact IMO or ISO safety-sign reproduction
Orange canvas with a black square and circle used as an active distress signal
Coastguard Tautiaki Moana logo, name, chevron, or bow-wave mark
identity_briefs.orientation: Use the lifeboat or wave emblem in a stable orthographic view with the bow facing the fly or toward open water. Keep white rescue symbols on green only as a design reference, not as an operational station sign.

palette.relief_red_reference: Pantone 186C is a New Zealand red reference, not a Red Cross authorization
palette.rescue_green: Deep green or sea-green chosen as an original flag colour, distinct from copied safety-sign layouts
palette.wave_blue: Royal or ocean blue derived from New Zealand maritime context
palette.white: White for stars and rescue silhouette

identity_briefs.uncertainty: The humanitarian state identity is fictional. Its emblem should read as a civic maritime seal, not a medical protective sign.

identity_briefs.concept: Isolationist southern refuge that turns navigation and closed waters into a guarded identity
recommended_motifs: Near-black or very deep blue field derived from documented silver-fern flag proposals and southern-night navigation
A compact four-star Southern Cross with white or muted silver stars, keeping the New Zealand four-star count
A single white or silver fern reduced to a hard, upright silhouette or shield-like frond
Optional narrow dark red seam or small red star accent recalling New Zealand maritime history without copying the national ensign
avoid: Exact black, white, and blue 2015 referendum flag reconstruction
Mauve, generic Polynesian tattoo, or invented tribal glyphs
Tino Rangatiratanga flag layout without a route-specific Maori partnership and review
Military skulls, radiation trefoils, or generic post-apocalypse symbols that replace New Zealand identity
identity_briefs.orientation: Keep the cross readable as a navigational constellation, with the fern vertical and visually contained. A closed refuge should look disciplined and maritime, not like a hazard warning.

palette.night_field: Near-black navy or deep ocean blue
palette.accent_red: Small Pantone 186C inspired accent only if needed

identity_briefs.uncertainty: No historical Southern Refuge flag exists. This is a fictional route synthesis using documented navigation and national motifs.

cultural_sensitivity.koru: The koru is a documented Maori art motif based on an unfurling fern and associated with renewal. It is not a generic spiral. Use it only as a route-specific motif with Maori partnership, and do not copy the Tino Rangatiratanga flag as decoration.
cultural_sensitivity.southern_cross_maori_variation: Te Ara records more than one Maori interpretation of the Southern Cross, including an anchor or sky canoe. Do not claim one interpretation for all iwi or attach a Maori reading without a source.
do_not_invent: Unnamed iwi patterns or generic Maori tattoo bands
Moko, carving, waka, pounamu, or kowhaiwhai as anonymous decoration
A new Te Reo name or translation without language review
A fictional rescue glyph presented as a traditional Maori symbol
cultural_sensitivity.recommended_route_rule: Default all three flags to Southern Cross, silver fern, maritime, and rescue references. Reserve a koru or Tino Rangatiratanga-derived treatment for an explicitly Maori-partnered route with separate cultural review.

must_show: One clean orthographic flag per identity
Flat fabric-free design with no flagpole, folds, sky, lighting, shadows, gradients, or perspective
Original vector-like geometry while preserving cited star count, colours, and motif orientation
must_not_show: Readable text, initials, slogans, seals, or invented heraldic claims
Union Jack or exact official ensign copy
Red Cross, Red Crescent, Red Crystal, Civil Defence logo, or Coastguard branding
Modern post-apocalypse props or a scene around a flag
required_evidence: Full ImageGen source master for each visually distinct identity
Prompt record naming every historical reference used
Comparison sheet with source master plus normal, medium, and small exports
Manifest entry with source URL, motif geometry, palette, orientation, rights note, and uncertainty
